bug_semantics: Any authenticated Winter CMS backend user could send a crafted My Account/My Settings save request for their own Backend\Models\User record and make the form behave as an administrative update form. The self-service action was deliberately exempted from backend.manage_users, while FormController treated the POST form_context value as authoritative. Selecting the update context caused normally excluded role, group, permission, and superuser fields to enter the widget save data, and the User model had no actor-aware authorization invariant before persistence. The user could therefore assign their own higher role/permissions or superuser status.
flaw_origin: Inherited pre-fork October CMS code supplied the unsafe combination's prerequisites in 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5 (the generic form context came from post('form_context') and the current-user save endpoint reused the administrative FormController). The smallest real commit that completed the advisory's any-backend-account attack path was the later, focused one-file commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9: it cleared Users::$requiredPermissions specifically for mysettings, exposing that unsafe save path to accounts without backend.manage_users. A later attempt in b121e03608135c921673d3b02d9ca293ca28c66a to pass the mysettings context did not close the issue because the posted form_context still overrode it.
ai_marker: No AI marker. `git cat-file commit 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9` shows human author and committer Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>, the sole message `Ref #306 - mysettings should be unrestricted by permissions`, and no commit body or trailers; there is no bot identity, Co-Authored-By AI trailer, or Generated-with trailer in the BIC commit object.
evidence: Advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-pgpf-m8m4-6cg6 states that a backend account with any level of access could modify its assigned roles/permissions and gives fixed package boundaries 1.0.477, 1.1.12, and 1.2.12. In the clone, `git show 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 -- modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` is a three-line addition that sets `$this->requiredPermissions = null` when the action is mysettings; `git show 0b8c8a0c0f616084c64747a31908efd1a470000b:modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` directly verifies that the immediate parent retains `$requiredPermissions = ['backend.manage_users']` and lacks that exception. Both `git log -S"requiredPermissions = null" -- modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` and `git log 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 -L 29,37:modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` identify 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9 as the origin of those lines. `git show 71a5dd67ab9e0d0da7caabd3fb5aaa3d86bb45e5:modules/backend/behaviors/FormController.php` shows `formGetContext()` returning `post('form_context', $this->context)`, and the same commit's Users.php and user fields show the self-save route and administrative permission fields. `git log e539b718d78197aa59944d6a16559f61e109d67b -L '/function myaccount_onSave/','/^    }/':modules/backend/controllers/Users.php` records b121e03608135c921673d3b02d9ca293ca28c66a passing a restricted self-service context, while the POST override remained. `git show d69e8415faafae409aaa046e1179b65364aad226` is the direct closing fix: FormController stops reading form_context from POST and makes the explicit context authoritative, while Backend\Models\User::beforeSave rejects self changes to role_id/is_superuser/permissions, requires backend.manage_users for other accounts, and reserves superuser changes for superusers. Equivalent backports are 7d6258703f1da2fdadb10e3a2d0c7d09ac2ae782 (1.0) and 76b57bccbb14b957b7981e43e0a5a969db220607 (1.1). `git tag --contains` returns d69e8415faafae409aaa046e1179b65364aad226 only for v1.2.12 among v1.2.11/v1.2.12, 7d6258703f1da2fdadb10e3a2d0c7d09ac2ae782 only for v1.0.477 among v1.0.476/v1.0.477, and 76b57bccbb14b957b7981e43e0a5a969db220607 only for v1.1.12 among v1.1.11/v1.1.12. The corresponding peeled patched tag commits are 7d6258703f1da2fdadb10e3a2d0c7d09ac2ae782, 76b57bccbb14b957b7981e43e0a5a969db220607, and b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313; v1.2.12's merge contains d69e8415faafae409aaa046e1179b65364aad226. `git tag --contains 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9` includes the earliest Winter tags checked (v1.0.437, v1.1.0, v1.2.0) and the last vulnerable tags v1.0.476, v1.1.11, and v1.2.11. First-party release notes https://wintercms.com/releases/v1.0.477 and https://wintercms.com/releases/v1.2.12 are dated 2026-02-20 and explicitly say protection against authenticated-backend-user privilege escalation was added.
reasoning: The initial 2014 import is a broad prerequisite, not the smallest commit completing the advisory-scoped flaw: before 94a4ccb6abccd025e7e201590999061574ffdeb9, an ordinary backend account without backend.manage_users could not enter the Users controller. The focused BIC deliberately removed that gate for self service without isolating the administrative form context or enforcing authorization in the model. Its parent therefore lacks the any-account attack path, and subsequent context-passing did not help while a crafted POST could replace the context. The 2026 fix closes both layers: it removes client authority over context and adds direct model authorization. Because the BIC commit object is an ordinary human-authored June 2014 commit with no AI/bot marker, the only supportable AI judgment is NOT_AI.
